pastWeek.title: Michigan State Fair
pastWeek.summary: A close-to-home Labor Day fair with livestock, creative arts, carnival rides, shopping, monster trucks and a demolition derby. Parking is free while space lasts.

pastWeek.title: Detroit Jazz Festival
pastWeek.price: Free general admission; VIP passes available
pastWeek.summary: The major free Labor Day weekend jazz festival returns with four days of national and Detroit artists on multiple downtown stages.

pastWeek.title: Silent Disco
pastWeek.summary: A headphone dance party with local electronic musician Ki5 DJing; headphones are provided, making it a free, delightfully odd downtown start to Friday.

pastWeek.title: D&D Adventurers League
pastWeek.summary: Play the official current Dungeons & Dragons campaign using fifth-edition rules; a strong organized option for a full evening of in-person games.

pastWeek.title: Drop-in Line Dancing
pastWeek.summary: A friendly, absolute-beginner session teaching three or more line dances; wear comfortable clothes and soft-soled shoes or boots.

pastWeek.title: Creature Encounters & Adult Open Hours
pastWeek.summary: A grown-up evening with close animal encounters, including a 7:30 presentation with a Highland cow, chicken, Flemish giant rabbit, and miniature donkey.

pastWeek.title: Tam White
pastWeek.registration: Tickets online or at the door if available
pastWeek.summary: Detroit-area stand-up comic, improv performer, and Hip-Prov host Tam White brings sharp material on marriage and her inability to twerk.

pastWeek.title: Friday Night Improv
pastWeek.summary: The 11 Non-Blondes house team performs a brisk Friday-night improv set in a brewery theater—an intimate alternative to a conventional comedy club.

pastWeek.title: Hiveside Chat
pastWeek.summary: Beekeeper Eileen Dickenson leads a hands-on introduction to biodynamic beekeeping at a working community farm.

pastWeek.title: The Side Questers
pastWeek.summary: Local author J.J. Kochmanski reads from and discusses a debut sci-fi fantasy about video-game side characters who set out to prove they can be heroes; signing follows.

pastWeek.title: Magic: The Gathering
pastWeek.summary: Choose a casual drop-in Commander table at 5 PM or organized Pauper and Standard rounds later in the evening; formats accommodate both social and competitive play.

pastWeek.title: Joshua Elwood & Friends
pastWeek.summary: Young West Michigan saxophonist Joshua Elwood leads an adventurous, warm jazz ensemble in North Star's genuinely small room.

pastWeek.title: Saturday Night Improv: Double Header
pastWeek.summary: Two local improv troupes take the brewery-theater stage, followed by Tony & Friends doing long-form comedy—an easy way to make a whole night of it.

pastWeek.title: The Ann Arbor Fall Beard Day Fest 2026
pastWeek.summary: An all-local, five-band rock bill featuring Van Haven, Redemption Road, LÜCID, Unholy Honor, and Keller—more intimate than a typical festival and a good late option.

pastWeek.title: First Saturday Contra Dance
pastWeek.summary: Jason Little calls participatory contra dances to the Pittsfield Open Band; arrive at 7 PM for the beginner introduction and bring clean dance shoes.

pastWeek.title: Rollie Tussing Trio
pastWeek.summary: Finger-style and slide guitar, trumpet and bass revive jazz, country blues and beautifully haunted songs from the 19th and early 20th centuries.

pastWeek.title: Open Board Games + Game Playtesting
pastWeek.summary: A friendly all-afternoon board-game room with instruction available; at 2 PM, test new board and card games from local Michigame Design Lab designers and give feedback.

pastWeek.title: Puzzle and Board Game Swap
pastWeek.summary: Pick up used puzzles and board games at a free community swap—an especially practical way to refresh a game shelf.

pastWeek.title: Phil Ogilvie’s Rhythm Kings
pastWeek.summary: A local 10-piece band plays the hot jazz of the 1920s and 30s—Jelly Roll Morton, King Oliver, Duke Ellington—for dancing or simply listening.

pastWeek.title: Extra Credit
pastWeek.summary: Three U-M researchers each give a 10-minute lecture, followed by experienced improvisers making a 10-minute comedy set from the topic—brainy, live, and delightfully strange.

pastWeek.title: Traditional Irish Session
pastWeek.summary: Listen in or bring an instrument to an open, acoustic Irish session at the pub—one of the most communal ways to hear live traditional music.

pastWeek.title: Twin Peaks Season 2
pastWeek.summary: Start a weekly big-screen run of David Lynch’s surreal second season as Dale Cooper’s investigation of Laura Palmer’s murder deepens.

pastWeek.title: Joe Summers & Pete Bullard
pastWeek.summary: Two veteran local guitarists play an intimate, free set of gypsy jazz tunes over dinner at a neighborhood Mexican restaurant.

pastWeek.title: Fiber Arts Drop-in
pastWeek.summary: Bring knitting, crochet, embroidery, or another portable fiber project to a relaxed, free Ypsilanti making circle.

pastWeek.title: Blind Pig Comedy
pastWeek.summary: A cheap Monday stand-up room featuring up to 15 aspiring comics from around the state, hosted by local comics and accompanied by free candy.

pastWeek.title: Game Night
pastWeek.summary: A friendly evening for board games, puzzles, miniature painting, and beginner-ready tabletop RPG one-shots at 6 PM; a strong go-solo option.

pastWeek.title: Gel Plate Printing
pastWeek.venue: Ann Arbor District Library — Downtown Secret Lab
pastWeek.summary: Use library paints, textures, and patterns to make one-of-a-kind monoprints in a low-pressure maker-space session for adults and teens.

pastWeek.title: Inside the Writer’s Study: Smell & Tell
pastWeek.summary: Writer and fragrance expert Michelle Krell Kydd guides a rare, playful smelling of seven mystery scents—part literature, part sensory detective work.

pastWeek.title: Shape Note Singing
pastWeek.summary: Learn this early American communal hymn-singing tradition through its distinctive shaped notation; songbooks are provided and no experience is needed.

pastWeek.title: Storytelling Nights
pastWeek.summary: A curated Ark night of top regional storytellers—Beverly Black, Steve Daut, Jeff Doyle, Jane Fink, Jennifer Otto, Barbara Schutzgruber, and Rich Swanson.

pastWeek.title: Alex Wand & Nelle Anderson
pastWeek.summary: Soprano-composer Nelle Anderson and guitarist Alex Wand blend opera, performance art, and unconventional-tuning improvisation, joined by L.A. violist Patrick Behnke.

pastWeek.title: Contemporary Directions Ensemble
pastWeek.summary: U-M graduate musicians explore repetition through shimmering contemporary chamber music, Rzewski’s playful Les Moutons de Panurge, and Steve Reich’s all-clapping classic.

pastWeek.title: Board Game Night
pastWeek.price: Free; food and drinks for purchase
pastWeek.summary: A relaxed after-work board-game table in a neighborhood food market; bring a favorite to share or join the games already on hand.

pastWeek.title: Board Game Night
pastWeek.price: Free; food and drinks for purchase
pastWeek.summary: An easy drop-in table for popular board games: use the house collection or bring your own while sampling mead and cider.

pastWeek.title: Happy Hour: Mikey Abbasspour
pastWeek.summary: Mikey Abbasspour’s free solo set moves among romantic boleros, classic songs, Celtic melodies, and literary folk influences.

pastWeek.title: Figure Drawing
pastWeek.summary: All skill levels draw from a live model in an intimate Ypsilanti arts space; bring your own supplies and expect light refreshments.

pastWeek.title: Jazz on the Trails
pastWeek.summary: A one-hour local jazz program along the Lower Rouge Trail. It is the lowest-travel plan-ahead option in this edition.

pastWeek.title: Bluegrass Jam Circle
pastWeek.summary: Bring an acoustic instrument or voice for a welcoming bluegrass circle; doors open at 6:30 PM, and weather questions can be checked by 3 PM.

pastWeek.title: An Adventure in Good Music: The Karl Haas Legacy
pastWeek.summary: Pianist Jeff Haas honors his WJR-radio-icon father with a documentary, a father-and-son composition, and Samuel Barber’s Summer Music by a local wind quintet.

pastWeek.title: Wednesday Night Swing
pastWeek.price: $5; free for members and lesson attendees
pastWeek.summary: Lindy Hop, Charleston, Balboa, and East Coast swing in a no-partner-needed weekly social; arrive early for the free beginner lesson.

pastWeek.title: Danny Elfman — Fall Tour 2026
pastWeek.summary: A rare career-spanning live set joining new rock material, Oingo Boingo songs and selections from Elfman's film and television scores.

pastWeek.title: Happy Hour: OUT Ensemble
pastWeek.summary: A new local wind quintet focused on expanding the representation of LGBTQ+ composers performs a compact free early-evening set.

pastWeek.title: (Sub)Surface
pastWeek.venue: Swords Into Plowshares Peace Center and Gallery
pastWeek.summary: Thirteen Detroit artists build work meant to be touched, heard and smelled as well as seen, centering access for blind and visually impaired visitors; programming includes talks and workshops.

pastWeek.title: Chicken Scratch Embroidery
pastWeek.summary: Adults and teens learn a vintage gingham embroidery technique that turns basic stitches into lace-like patterns.

pastWeek.title: Repairsday Thursday
pastWeek.summary: Bring a broken object to a collaborative volunteer repair night; repairs are not guaranteed, but practical tinkering and learning are the point.

pastWeek.title: Adult Forest Therapy Walk
pastWeek.summary: A slow, restorative one-mile guided walk designed to help adults reconnect with the natural world.

pastWeek.title: Nerd Nite
pastWeek.summary: Three lively 20-minute talks on unexpected subjects make a social, brainy evening; presenter topics are listed by the organizer.

pastWeek.title: Pitch-a-Friend
pastWeek.summary: Friends give short, clean slide presentations introducing eligible singles, followed by mingling; the LGBTQ+-friendly format also welcomes platonic connection.

pastWeek.title: Walk Right In
pastWeek.summary: The Ann Arbor Film Festival brings award-winning short films outdoors; bring a blanket or lawn chair, with food and drinks available for purchase.

pastWeek.title: Live Trivia
pastWeek.price: Free to play; food and drinks for purchase
pastWeek.summary: A relaxed live-trivia night in a mead-and-cider room, ideal for a group or an easy solo outing.

pastWeek.title: Square Dance: University Musical Society Ypsi Freighthouse Residency
pastWeek.summary: Detroit Square Dance Society leads taught, rehearsed square and line dances with non-gendered calling and live music.

pastWeek.title: The Claudettes
pastWeek.summary: Chicago’s self-styled garage-cabaret quartet mixes New Orleans piano blues, rockabilly, punk energy, and 1960s soul in an intimate Ark setting.

today.title: The Street Art Encounter
today.summary: A downtown street-art program with artists working in public and opportunities to encounter new work across Main Street.

today.title: D&D Adventurers League
today.summary: A scheduled Adventurers League tabletop session at the local game shop.

today.title: Asian Chip Taste Test

today.title: Bluegrass Friday: Pontiac Trail Blazers ft. Gregory Stovetop

easyAnswer: On September 11, try an Asian chip tasting at AADL, square dance with live strings at Three Cedars Farm, or catch Rainbow Girls at The Ark. On September 12, release tagged monarchs at Leslie Science & Nature Center, join a water-history walk, or hear the Django Reinhardt Festival at The Ark.
